en: The *Dhāraṇī-vidhi-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of South India by Imperial Decree.
At that time, Vināyaka gathered a great assembly on Mount Kīla; Brahmā himself...
Śakra-devānām-indra and others among the gods,
as well as immeasurable billions of spirits and deities,
rose from their seats.
Having prostrated and paid homage to Maheśvara, he requested him to speak:
"I now wish to proclaim a one-syllable mantra for the benefit of sentient beings;
I pray that you will grant your approval and listen to what I have to say."
The devas said, "Excellent! It is just as you have spoken.
Vināyakas, having heard this, were filled with joy and leaped for gladness.
They then uttered the one-syllable mantra of the Vināyakas, which says: [VĪṂ].
Oṃ kha-kha-ri oṃ ha hūṃ phaṭ ṭha. To perform this rite, one must first fashion an image, using either white brass, gold, silver, copper, birch wood, or other such materials.
Carve each into its respective form:
the two bodies of husband and wife standing in an embrace of union,
both having the heads of elephants and the bodies of humans.
The price for the creation of the image must not be returned.
Once the image has been completed,
on the first day of the waxing moon—
Within a clean room, one should prepare a circular mandala using purified cow dung,
of whatever size is desired.
One should then take one *śroṇa* of sesame oil.
Using the aforementioned mantra,
consecrate the pure oil one hundred and eight times to warm it.
Then, place the warmed oil in a clean copper vessel.
Thereafter, place the image in oil within a copper basin and install it inside the mandala; then,
using a clean copper spoon or ladle, skim the oil.
One should consecrate the crowns of the heads of the two images one hundred and eight times.
Thereafter, every day, one should further recite the mantra over the old oil one hundred and eight times and sprinkle it upon them seven times within a single day.
Perform four recitations at dawn and three at noon, making seven in total.
Practice this ritual in this manner for up to seven days;
whatever one’s heart desires will be fulfilled according to one’s wishes.
While performing the formal oil-consecration, one should repeatedly make aspirational prayers.
One should prepare dough-balls mixed with ghee and honey,
along with radish roots and cups of fermented vinegar and grain-based liquor.
Thus, one must personally consume the food offered daily;
only then will one obtain the necessary vital strength.
At that time, Vināyakas...
Leading nine thousand eight hundred great ghost kings,
we travel through the three thousandfold world-systems;
the supernatural powers we exercise are sovereign and unimpeded.
Having traveled throughout all directions to serve and protect the Triple Gem,
and having already brought benefit to sentient beings through great compassion,
they addressed the World-Honored One in unison, saying:
By virtue of my sovereign supernormal powers,
I am called Vinaranaga,
and I am also named Vinayaka.
It is also called Vaimanaka,
and it is also called Mahāvinayaka;
thus, the names by which the four continents are designated all differ.
I have another name for the supramundane;
by means of a miraculous transformation, I ascended into the void and spoke this verse:
"I possess a subtle and wondrous Dharma, Which is exceedingly rare in the world."
For all sentient beings who uphold [this], their vows shall be fulfilled.
I practice in accordance with worldly ways and manifest rare and wondrous deeds within the world.
I can grant their wishes: for those who seek fame, they shall attain high office.
I shall cause the king to summon those who seek the extraordinary treasures of the world,
who amass worldly wealth and profit, whose households abound in the seven precious gems rare to all the world,
and those who seek the beauty of form.
When one makes this vow, it is as if one has already arrived;
there is no need to speak of distance or proximity, nobility or lowliness, or ease or difficulty.
For those who direct their sincere heart toward me, I shall cause them to be free from the sickness and suffering of sentient beings within a mere moment.
For those afflicted by possession by spirits, madness, scabies, or leprosy,
and for those harmed by the hundred kinds of diseases, poisons, and various misfortunes—
none shall fail to be liberated if they recite my dhāraṇī, even when traveling alone in dark and obscure places.
Relying on me, all shall be fearless; even if bandits suddenly invade, I shall cause them all to bind themselves.
If one desires natural merit, or seeks a woman, may the husband’s heart obtain that woman.
I shall surely cause you to love one another; those who are aggressive and arrogant in this world, I shall completely subdue.
May you roam in carefree joy, entirely lacking for nothing, and may every wish be fulfilled.
May all who encounter me be fully satisfied; even if various evils come to assail me, may I cause them to follow my will.
May I be able to provide protection for all, so that where I dwell there shall be auspiciousness and prosperity, and every home shall be pure and peaceful.
Men and women shall attain illustrious fame; husband and wife shall be harmonious and united.
To those who uphold me in the highest manner, I grant the status of a king among men;
to those who uphold me in the middling manner, I grant the position of imperial preceptor.
Those who uphold me in an inferior manner will enjoy inexhaustible wealth and honor;
they will constantly desire to amuse themselves, never lacking in full satisfaction.
Their servants and slaves will form a multitude, and beautiful women will fill their streets and courtyards.
Wandering with mastery, able to appear and disappear at will,
entering and exiting without obstruction— none can fathom me;
within the three realms, I have attained sovereignty through my supernormal powers.
The rare events of my descent into the world, all these I have performed;
were one to speak of my capabilities, they could not be exhausted even at the end of an eon.
Those who uphold my dhāraṇī—I shall appear before them all.
Husband, wife, and their retinue shall receive protection accordingly.
When I am traveling, if they recite my name,
I will immediately arrive to lead them past dangerous places— vast oceans and great rivers.
In deep mountains and perilous passes, amidst lions, elephants, tigers, wolves, venomous insects,
and various malevolent spirits, by holding this [mantra], one shall be secure;
should there be any who cause harm, their heads shall be split into seven pieces.
"May their lifespans all be long and far-reaching, and may fortune and merit spontaneously arrive.
At that time, after Vināyakaga had spoken this verse,
he addressed the people of the world, saying:
The method for reciting the Lokeśvara Dhāraṇī is now explained.
It provides the supreme protection for sentient beings,
and all their aspirations shall be fulfilled accordingly.
One must recite and maintain this [mantra] day and night for one hundred thousand times, up to two hundred thousand times.
Then, as described, one shall immediately ascend into the void.
The mantra is spoken as follows:
The monk Jingyan of Henan Jiaxing, No.
49, completed a second collation against the imperial original. Respected Teaching.
